summary: Configured /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker as the enabled systemd service inventory-worker under the dedicated inventorysvc account. CentOS Stream 10 and kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 were preserved. After one safe node reboot, the boot ID changed and the service automatically recovered under inventorysvc.
actions_performed: Created the locked, non-login inventorysvc system account and private home directory.
Created, validated, enabled, and started inventory-worker.service using native systemd.
Configured automatic failure restart and systemd security hardening.
Rebooted node1 exactly once and verified post-reboot persistence and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Run the worker as managed service inventory-worker under dedicated inventorysvc account
evidence.summary: inventorysvc exists as a dedicated non-login account; the unit is enabled and active; systemd and process output show /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker running as inventorysvc.

evidence.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Both pre- and post-reboot checks report CentOS Stream 10 (Coughlan) and kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory node1 restart and recovery sequence
evidence.summary: Healthy baseline used boot ID a70d7f83-6867-4c91-851d-7a1228689bb3; reboot was acknowledged and the node became temporarily unavailable; recovered boot ID is ad5d480e-6da4-4163-94ee-4b9a397fd788. After recovery, inventory-worker is enabled and active with PID 842 running as inventorysvc, and current-boot journal confirms successful startup.
